guides.title: Subscription System Management Guide
guides.content:
Subscription System Overview

What This Guide Covers

This guide explains how PayTrade's subscription system works end-to-end — from creating plans and items to managing the public pricing page. It is intended for admin users only.

The subscription system controls which features and limits each user or business gets based on their plan. It consists of several interconnected components:

Key Components

ComponentPurposeAdmin Page
Subscription PlansDefine the tier levels (Free, Basic, Standard, etc.) with pricing and billing cyclesSubscriptions → Manage Plans
Subscription ItemsDefine specific features/limits (e.g., number of projects, trust accounts) that can be assigned to plansSubscriptions → Manage Items
CouponsPromotional discount codes synced with StripeSubscriptions → Manage Coupons
Manage ProfilesView and manage active user/business subscriptionsSubscriptions → Manage Profiles
Billing HistoryReview all payment transactions and download invoicesSubscriptions → Billing History
Pricing TableEdit the feature comparison grid shown on the public /pricing pageSubscriptions → Pricing Table

How Plans Work

Subscription plans define the tiers available to users. Each plan has a name, description, price, billing cycle, and a set of items that determine the feature limits for that plan.

Important: Stripe Integration

Plans are synced with Stripe. When you create or update a plan, it creates a corresponding product and price in Stripe. Always verify changes appear correctly in both PayTrade and the Stripe dashboard.

Plan Types

Plan TypeDescription
FreeDefault plan for new sign-ups. Limited features, no payment required.
PaidPremium plans (Basic, Standard, Advanced, Pro Audit) with monthly or annual billing through Stripe.

Managing Plans

1
Navigate to Manage Plans

In the admin sidebar, go to Subscriptions → Manage Plans. You will see a list of all current plans.

2
View Plan Details

Click on any plan to see its full details, including the assigned items (feature limits), pricing, and Stripe sync status.

3
Edit a Plan

Click the edit icon on any plan to change its name, description, pricing, billing cycle, or status. You can switch between Current and Archived views using the tabs at the top.

4
Add a New Plan

Click the Add Plan button to create a new subscription tier. Fill in the plan name, type (Free/Paid), price, billing interval, and then assign items to define what features and limits this plan includes.

How Subscription Items Work

Subscription items are the individual features or limits that make up a plan. They define what a subscriber can do and how much of each feature they get.

Item Limit Types

Limit TypeHow It WorksExample
NumericSets a specific count limit. Can be set to "Unlimited" for premium tiers.Projects: Free = 1, Basic = 3, Standard = 10, Advanced = Unlimited
DropdownEnables or disables a feature. Typically Yes/No or Active/Inactive.Trust Accounting: Free = No, Standard = Yes

Managing Items

1
Navigate to Manage Items

Go to Subscriptions → Manage Items. This shows all defined items with their limit types and status.

2
Create or Edit Items

Each item has a name, description, limit type (Numeric or Dropdown), and status (Active/Inactive). When creating an item, choose the limit type carefully — Numeric items allow you to set specific counts per plan, while Dropdown items are simple on/off toggles.

3
Assign Items to Plans

After creating items, go back to Manage Plans, edit a plan, and assign items to it. For each item you assign, you can set the specific limit value (e.g., 5 projects, or Unlimited).

How Items Control Features

When a user is on a plan, the system checks the items assigned to that plan to determine their limits. For example, if the "Projects" item is set to 3 for the Basic plan, then Basic subscribers can only create up to 3 projects. This enforcement happens in real-time throughout the application.

How Plans and Items Connect

Understanding the relationship between plans and items is essential for managing subscriptions effectively:

ConceptExplanation
Plan → ItemsEach plan has a list of assigned items with specific values. Example: the "Standard" plan includes "Projects" item set to 10, "Trust Accounts" set to 5, and "Compliance Reports" set to Unlimited.
Item Values Per PlanThe same item (e.g., "Projects") can have different values on different plans. This is how tiers are differentiated.
Unlimited OverrideFor numeric items, you can set a plan's value to "Unlimited" instead of a number. This is typically used for higher-tier plans.

Managing the Public Pricing Table

The Pricing Table Editor controls what users see on the public /pricing page. This is a separate system from plan items — it manages the visual feature comparison grid that helps users decide which plan to choose.

Important Distinction

Plan Items control the actual feature limits enforced by the system. Pricing Table Features control the comparison grid shown on the website. They are related but managed separately — changes to the pricing table do NOT change actual plan limits, and vice versa.

Updating the Pricing Table

1
Navigate to the Pricing Table Editor

Go to Subscriptions → Pricing Table. You will see a list of all features currently displayed on the /pricing page.

2
Edit Feature Values

Click the edit (pencil) icon on any row to modify the feature name or the value shown for each plan column. Values work as follows:

  • "true" — Displays a green checkmark meaning "included"
  • "false" — Displays a red cross meaning "not included"
  • Any other text — Displays the text as-is (e.g., "Up to 3", "Unlimited", "Coming soon")
3
Add a New Feature Row

Click the + Add Feature button to add a new row. Enter the feature name and the value for each plan tier (Basic, Standard, Advanced, Pro Audit). The new row is added at the bottom and can be reordered.

4
Reorder Features

Use the up/down arrow buttons to reorder features. The display order on the public pricing page matches this order.

5
Preview Before Saving

Click the Preview button to see how the pricing table will look to users on the public website. This shows the exact rendering with checkmarks, crosses, and text values.

6
Delete a Feature

Click the trash icon to remove a feature row. You will be asked to confirm before it is permanently deleted.

Pricing Table Value Examples
FeatureBasicStandardAdvancedPro Audit
Trust Accountingfalse (cross)true (tick)true (tick)true (tick)
ProjectsUp to 1Up to 5UnlimitedUnlimited
Bank Feedsfalse (cross)Coming soonComing soonComing soon

Managing Coupons

Coupons provide discounts on subscription plans. They are synced with Stripe and can be used during the checkout process.

1
Navigate to Manage Coupons

Go to Subscriptions → Manage Coupons.

2
Create a Coupon

Click Add Coupon and fill in the discount percentage and duration in months. The coupon is automatically created in Stripe as well.

3
Archive or Deactivate

Expired or unwanted coupons can be archived. Switch to the Archived tab to view them. Archived coupons cannot be redeemed by users.

Managing Subscriber Profiles

The Manage Profiles page shows all businesses with active or cancelled subscriptions.

1
View Subscriber Details

Go to Subscriptions → Manage Profiles. You can search by business name or filter by status (Active/Cancelled).

2
Cancel a Subscription

If needed, you can cancel a business's subscription from this page. This will also cancel it in Stripe. The business will retain access until the end of their current billing period.

Billing History

1
View Transactions

Go to Subscriptions → Billing History to see a list of all payment transactions. You can filter by business profile, payment status (Paid/Failed), and date range.

2
Download Invoices

Each transaction includes a link to download the invoice PDF directly.

3
Export Data

Use the export button to download billing data as Excel or PDF for accounting and reporting purposes.

Common Tasks Quick Reference

TaskWhere to GoSteps
Change a plan's priceManage Plans → EditEdit the plan, update the price, save. Changes sync to Stripe.
Add a feature limit to a planManage Items + Manage PlansFirst create the item in Manage Items if it doesn't exist, then edit the plan and assign the item with the desired value.
Update what's shown on the /pricing pagePricing TableEdit, add, or remove features. Use Preview to verify before leaving the page.
Create a promotional discountManage Coupons → AddSet percentage discount and duration in months. Coupon code is created in Stripe automatically.
Cancel a user's subscriptionManage ProfilesFind the business, click Cancel Subscription. Access continues until billing period ends.
Check if a payment failedBilling HistoryFilter by status "Failed" to see all unsuccessful payment attempts.
Caution: Things to Avoid
  • Do not delete plans that have active subscribers. Archive them instead.
  • Do not change plan pricing without notice — existing subscribers keep their current rate until renewal, but Stripe will charge the new rate at next renewal.
  • The Pricing Table is display-only — editing it does not change actual feature limits. Always update both the pricing table AND plan items if you want changes reflected everywhere.
  • Coupon codes cannot be reused once they are archived/deleted in Stripe.

guides.title: Admin Dashboard and Navigation
guides.content:
Admin Dashboard and Navigation

The admin panel provides full control over the PayTrade platform. This guide is for Portal Admins and Restricted Portal Admins only.

Admin dashboard page

Admin Dashboard

What You See on This Page

ComponentWhat It Shows
New Users CountNumber of users who registered recently
New Businesses CountNumber of new business profiles created
Notices PendingSystem-wide count of notices that need attention
Compliance IssuesPlatform-wide compliance problems requiring review
Failed TransactionsSubscription payment failures that need investigation
Trust Accounting IssuesTrust accounts with reconciliation or balance problems
Quick Access LinksShortcuts to all major admin sections

Admin Navigation

The admin sidebar provides access to all management functions:

  • Users — Manage platform users, block/unblock, reset passwords
  • Businesses — View and manage registered businesses
  • Admin Users — Manage admin accounts and permissions
  • Groups — Define permission groups for admin roles
  • Subscriptions — Manage plans, items, coupons, and billing
  • Content Management — FAQ, email templates
  • Blog — Create and manage blog posts
  • Resource Guides — Manage educational resources
  • How-to Guides — Manage platform guides (like this one!)
  • Community — Moderate discussions and product ideas
  • Notices — View all platform notices
  • Compliance — Platform-wide compliance overview
  • Communication — Send system-wide emails
  • Masters — Manage dropdown values and system constants
  • Holidays — Configure public holidays that affect payment deadlines
  • Activity Log — Full audit trail of admin actions

guides.title: Managing Users and Businesses (Admin)
guides.content:
Managing Users and Businesses

A guide for admins on managing platform users and business profiles.

Admin Users management page

Users Management Page

What You See on This Page

ComponentWhat It Shows
User NameFirst and last name of the registered user
EmailThe user's login email address
PhoneContact phone number
CompanyThe primary company the user belongs to
StatusActive, Blocked, or Unverified
SubscriptionWhich plan the user's company is on (Basic, Standard, Advanced, Pro Audit)
ContactedWhether an admin has marked this user as contacted (useful for sales follow-up)
ActionsEdit, block/unblock, reset password, login as user, generate bot users

Key Admin Actions

Editing a User

Click "Edit" to update a user's details, change their status, or modify their subscription settings.

Blocking/Unblocking

Click "Block" to prevent a user from logging in. They will see an error message when attempting to access their account. Click "Unblock" to restore access.

Resetting a Password

Click "Reset Password" to generate a new password and send it to the user's email address. The user can then change it after logging in.

Login As User (Portal Admin Only)

This powerful feature lets a Portal Admin log in as any user to troubleshoot issues. You will be prompted to enter your admin password for security. Use this carefully — all actions taken will be logged.

Admin Business management page

Business Management

What You See on This Page

ComponentWhat It Shows
Business NameThe registered company name
ABNAustralian Business Number
Entity TypeBusiness, Sole Trader, or Personal
QBCC NumberQBCC license number (if applicable)
VerifiedWhether the business has been verified by admin
ActionsEdit details, view linked users, manage verification status
Important: The "Login As User" feature should only be used for legitimate troubleshooting. All actions taken while logged in as a user are recorded in the activity log.

guides.title: Managing Subscriptions and Billing (Admin)
guides.content:
Managing Subscriptions and Billing

Control subscription plans, plan items, coupons, and view billing history across the platform.

Admin Subscriptions management page

Subscription Plans

What You See on This Page

ComponentWhat It Shows
Plan NameThe name of the subscription tier (Basic, Standard, Advanced, Pro Audit)
Price (Monthly/Yearly)The cost of the plan per billing period
StatusActive or Archived
Trial PeriodNumber of days for the free trial period (if applicable)
ActionsEdit pricing, view plan details, archive/restore

Plan Items

Plan items define what features and limits each plan includes:

Admin Subscription Items management page

What You See on This Page

ComponentWhat It Shows
Item NameThe feature name (e.g., "Users", "Projects", "Trusts")
PlanWhich subscription plan this item belongs to
Limit ValueThe numeric limit for this feature (e.g., 5 users, 10 projects)
Is UnlimitedIf checked, no limit is enforced for this feature on this plan
StatusActive or Archived

Managing Coupons

Coupons provide discounts on subscription plans. They are synced with Stripe.

1
Navigate to Manage Coupons

Go to Subscriptions > Manage Coupons.

2
Create a Coupon

Enter the coupon code, discount type (percentage or fixed), discount amount, and expiry date.

3
The coupon syncs to Stripe

When saved, the coupon is created in Stripe and can be applied during checkout.

Billing History

View all subscription transactions, including successful payments, failed charges, and refunds. Use this to investigate billing issues reported by users.

Tip: When changing plan pricing, note that existing subscribers on the old price will not be automatically updated. They will see the new price at their next renewal unless manually adjusted.

guides.title: Content Management and Community Moderation (Admin)
guides.content:
Content Management and Community Moderation

Manage all platform content including FAQs, blog posts, resource guides, how-to guides, and community moderation.

FAQ Management

Admin FAQ management page

Create and manage FAQ entries that appear on the public FAQ page. Each FAQ has a question, answer (rich text), category, and publish status.

Blog Management

Admin Blog management page

Create and manage blog articles. Each post has a title, content (rich text editor), category, banner image, tags, and publish status. Published posts appear at /blog.

Community Moderation

Admin Community Discussions page

What You See on This Page

ComponentWhat It Shows
Discussion TitleThe title of the discussion thread
AuthorWho started the discussion
CategoryThe topic category
AnswersNumber of answers/responses
StatusActive, Reported, or Deleted
ActionsView, delete, review reported content, generate bot answers

Community Bot Controls

Admins have special buttons to generate AI-powered content:

  • "Generate Bot Users" (Users page) — Creates AI-generated user personas with realistic Australian construction industry profiles
  • "Generate Bot Question" (Discussions page header) — Uses OpenAI GPT-4o to generate a realistic discussion with question and answer
  • "Generate Bot Answers" (per discussion row) — Generates AI answers for a specific active discussion
Tip: The community bot also runs automatically on Monday, Wednesday, and Friday at 9 AM UTC, generating new questions and answers to keep the community active.

guides.title: Subscription Plans and Upgrading
guides.content:

Understand the differences between PayTrade plans and how to upgrade for more features.

PayTrade pricing page

ABA Generation-YesYesYes
Bank Feeds-YesYesYes
Delegate Authority--YesYes
Xero Integration--YesYes
Audit Export---Yes

How to Upgrade

1
Navigate to Subscription Settings

Click your profile icon > Manage Subscriptions, or go directly to the Upgrade Plan page.

2
Choose a Plan

Select Billing Period

guides.title: Personal Settings and Security
guides.content:
Personal Settings and Security

Update your profile information, change your password, and review your account activity.

Personal Information page

Personal Information

Navigate to your profile icon in the top-right corner and select "Personal Info" to update:

  • First name and last name
  • Phone number
  • Address (with Google Places autocomplete)
  • Occupation and position title
  • Profile photo

Sign-in & Security page

Sign-in & Security

Navigate to "Sign-in & Security" to manage your login credentials:

Changing Your Password

1
Enter Current Password

For security, you must verify your identity by entering your current password.

2
Enter New Password

Create a new password meeting the complexity requirements: 8+ characters, uppercase, lowercase, number, and special character.

3
Confirm and Save

Re-enter the new password and click Save. You will remain logged in.

Activity Log page

Activity Log

The Activity Log shows a complete audit trail of all actions taken on your account:

What You See on This Page

ComponentWhat It Shows
TimestampWhen the action occurred
ActionWhat was done (e.g., "Created project", "Submitted claim", "Updated contract")
DetailsSpecific details about the action
IP AddressThe IP address the action was performed from
Tip: Review your Activity Log periodically to check for any unexpected actions, especially if you share account access with team members.

guides.title: User Access and Invitations
guides.content:
User Access and Invitations

Invite team members to your company, manage their roles, and control what they can access.

User Roles Within a Company

What You See on This Page

ComponentWhat It Shows
Primary AdminThe person who created the company profile. Has full control over all settings, users, and data.
AdminElevated permissions — can manage users, projects, and most business functions. Cannot delete the company or change billing.
Standard UserRegular team member with access to day-to-day operations like creating claims and viewing projects. Cannot manage other users.
Basic UserLimited access — can view their own data and perform basic tasks only.

Inviting Team Members

1
Navigate to User Access

Go to Company > User Access in the sidebar.

2
Click "Add User"

Click the add button to invite a new team member.

3
Enter Their Details

Provide their email address, name, and the role you want to assign.

4
Set Permissions

Configure granular permissions: manage projects, manage trust payments, manage users, manage company, manage subscriptions.

5
Send Invitation

The system sends an email invitation. The user can sign up (if new) or accept the invitation (if they have an existing PayTrade account).

Managing Invitations

Go to Company > Invitations to view pending invitations. You can:

  • See which invitations are still pending
  • Resend invitation emails
  • Revoke invitations that are no longer needed
Important: Your subscription plan limits the number of users. Basic plans allow 1 user, Standard allows 5, and Advanced/Pro Audit allow unlimited users. You will receive an upgrade prompt if you try to exceed your limit.

guides.title: Managing Variations
guides.content:
Managing Variations

Variations track changes to contract scope and value. This guide explains how to create and manage them.

Variations list page

What Are Variations?

In construction, a variation is a change to the original contract — it could be additional work, reduced scope, or modified specifications. Variations affect the contract sum and need to be formally tracked.

Variations List Page

What You See on This Page

ComponentWhat It Shows
Variation Name/ReferenceA unique identifier for the variation
ContractThe contract this variation modifies
AmountThe financial impact — positive for additional work, negative for reduced scope
StatusDraft, Submitted, Approved, Rejected, or Completed
ActionsView, edit, or approve the variation

Creating a Variation

1
Navigate to Variations

Click "Variations" in the sidebar menu.

2
Click "Add Variation"

Click the add button in the top-right corner.

3
Select the Contract

Choose which contract this variation applies to.

4
Enter Details

Fill in the variation description, the financial amount (positive or negative), and any supporting documentation.

5
Submit for Approval

Save the variation and submit it for approval by the relevant party.

Once a variation is approved, the contract's "Adjusted Contract Sum" automatically updates to reflect the change.

Tip: Keep variations well-documented with descriptions and supporting files. This creates a clear audit trail and helps prevent disputes about scope changes.

guides.title: New User Onboarding Flow
guides.content:
New User Onboarding Flow

A complete guide for new users — from registration to creating your first project and processing your first payment.

PayTrade home page — your starting point

Week 1: Registration & Setup

Day 1: Create Your Account

1
Sign Up

Visit paytrade.app and click "Sign up for free". Complete the multi-step registration process.

2
Set Up Your Business Profile

Enter your company details, ABN, and QBCC license number. Upload your logo.

3
Explore the Dashboard

Familiarise yourself with the dashboard layout, sidebar navigation, and quick action links.

Day 2-3: Add Your Contacts

4
Add Clients & Suppliers

Go to Clients & Suppliers > Add. Enter your principals, head contractors, subcontractors, and suppliers.

5
Consider Upgrading

If you need more than 1 project or 2 trust accounts, review the pricing plans and upgrade your subscription.

Week 2: First Project

6
Create Your First Project

Go to Projects > Add Project. Enter the project details and check PTA eligibility.

7
Set Up Contracts

Go to Contracts > Add Contract. Link the contract to your project and the relevant client/supplier.

8
Open Trust Accounts

If PTA/RTA eligible, create the required trust accounts under Bank Accounts.

9
Generate Opening Notices

Create and send QBCC TA1 notices for each new trust account.

Week 3+: Ongoing Operations

10
Submit Payment Claims

As work is completed, create payment claims under Pay Apps.

11
Record Payments

When payments are made or received, record them against the relevant claims.

12
Upload & Reconcile

Download your bank statement CSV and upload it. Match transactions to claims.

13
Monthly Reconciliation

At month end, create a reconciliation record for each trust account.

14
Monitor Compliance

Check the Compliance dashboard regularly to ensure everything is in order.

Tip: Don't try to set up everything at once. Start with one project and learn the workflow, then expand to additional projects as you become comfortable with the system.

guides.title: Trust Account Lifecycle
guides.content:
Trust Account Lifecycle

From opening to closing — the complete lifecycle of a trust account in PayTrade.

Phase 1: Eligibility Check

1
Create a Project

When creating a project, the system checks if the head contract sum exceeds the BIF Act threshold for a PTA.

2
PTA Eligibility Determined

If eligible, the project is marked "PTA Eligibility: Yes". The compliance module begins monitoring.

Phase 2: Account Opening

3
Open the Trust Account

Navigate to Bank Accounts > Add Account. Select "Project Trust Account" or "Retention Trust Account" and enter your bank details.

4
Link to Project

Associate the trust account with the relevant project.

5
Generate TA1 Notice

Navigate to Notices > Add Notice. Generate a QBCC TA1 (Account Opening) notice. This is mandatory.

6
Send TA1

Send the TA1 notice to QBCC and all relevant beneficiaries via email.

Phase 3: Active Use

During the project lifecycle, the trust account is used for:

  • Receiving project payments from the principal
  • Making payments to subcontractors and suppliers
  • Holding retention money (if RTA)
  • Monthly reconciliations
  • Generating journal entries and ledger records
  • Generating TA4 (Part Payment) and TA5 (Nil Return) notices as needed

Phase 4: Account Closure

7
Complete All Payments

Ensure all claims are paid and all retention released.

8
Final Reconciliation

Perform a final monthly reconciliation ensuring the balance is zero.

9
Generate TA2 Notice

Generate a QBCC TA2 (Account Closing) notice.

10
Archive the Account

Move the trust account to "Archived" status. All records are retained for 7 years.

Tip: Even after a trust account is archived, its full history — journals, reconciliations, notices, and audit trail — remains accessible for the statutory 7-year retention period.

guides.title: End-to-End Payment Flow
guides.content:
End-to-End Payment Flow

A complete walkthrough of the payment process from claim submission through to bank reconciliation.

Overview

This guide follows a typical payment scenario: a subcontractor claims payment from a head contractor for completed work, and the head contractor processes the payment through a Project Trust Account.

Phase 1: Setup (Prerequisites)

Before any payment can flow, the following must already exist:

  • A Project has been created with PTA eligibility determined
  • A Contract links the project to the client/supplier with payment terms defined
  • A Project Trust Account (PTA) has been opened and linked to the project
  • If retention applies, a Retention Trust Account (RTA) is also set up
  • QBCC TA1 (Account Opening) notices have been generated and sent

Phase 2: Claim Submission

1
Subcontractor Creates a Claim

The subcontractor navigates to Pay Apps > Add Claim, selects the contract, enters the claim amount and description, and submits.

2
System Calculates Retention

Based on the contract's retention percentage, the system automatically calculates and displays the retention amount that will be withheld.

3
Claim Appears for Head Contractor

The claim shows up in the head contractor's Billable tab, and in their Payments To Do dashboard widget.

Phase 3: Claim Review & Payment

4
Head Contractor Reviews

The head contractor opens the claim from their Billable tab, reviews the amount and supporting documents.

5
Payment Recorded

From the claim view, the head contractor clicks "Add Payment", enters the payment details (amount, date, reference), and saves.

6
S75 Generated

An S75 Supporting Statement is automatically generated. This must accompany the payment as a legal requirement.

7
Retention Withheld

The retention portion is separated and tracked in the Retention List. If an RTA exists, the retained amount should be deposited there.

Phase 4: Bank Reconciliation

8
Upload Bank Statement

Once the payment clears the bank, the head contractor downloads a CSV bank statement and uploads it via Bank Accounts > Upload Transactions.

9
Match Transaction

Navigate to Match Transactions. Find the bank transaction that corresponds to the claim payment and match them together.

10
Ledger Updated

The trust account ledger updates automatically. The transaction is no longer "unmatched" on the dashboard.

Phase 5: Monthly Reconciliation

11
Create Reconciliation Record

At month end, navigate to Trust Accounting > Reconciliation Records > Add. Enter the bank statement closing balance.

12
Compare Balances

The system compares the bank balance with the ledger balance. Any differences are explained by outstanding unmatched items.

13
Save and Confirm

Save the reconciliation. The Compliance dashboard updates to show the trust account is reconciled for this period.

Important: Every step in this flow is tracked for compliance purposes. Skipping steps (like failing to reconcile or not sending S75 statements) will trigger compliance alerts.

guides.title: Using the Community Forum
guides.content:
Using the Community Forum

Connect with other construction professionals, ask questions about trust accounting and the BIF Act, and suggest new features.

Community home page

Community Sections

What You See on This Page

ComponentWhat It Shows
DiscussionsA Q&A forum where users can ask questions and share answers about trust accounting, BIF Act compliance, and construction industry best practices.
Product IdeasA feature request board where users can submit ideas for improving PayTrade and vote on others' suggestions.

Starting a Discussion

1
Navigate to Community

Click "Community" in the sidebar or the top navigation menu.

2
Click "Start a Discussion"

Click the button to create a new discussion topic.

3
Select a Category

Choose the most relevant category for your question.

4
Write Your Question

Enter a clear title and detailed description. Include any relevant context about your project or situation.

5
Submit

Click "Submit" to post your discussion. Other users can now see and respond to it.

Interacting with Content

  • Answer: Reply to a discussion with your answer or insight
  • Like: Show appreciation for helpful answers by clicking the like button
  • Best Answer: The answer with the most likes is automatically highlighted as the "Best Answer"
  • Vote (Product Ideas): Upvote feature requests you want to see implemented
  • Report: Flag inappropriate content as "Inappropriate" or "Spam"
Tip: The Community is available on all plans, including the free Basic plan. It's a great resource for getting answers about BIF Act compliance from experienced professionals.

guides.title: Connecting Xero to PayTrade
guides.content:
Connecting Xero to PayTrade

Sync your accounting data between PayTrade and Xero automatically. Available on Advanced and Pro Audit plans.

Integrations page

What Xero Integration Does

  • Sync Contacts: Import your Xero contacts as PayTrade clients and suppliers
  • Sync Invoices: Keep invoices in sync between both platforms
  • Sync Bills: Bills from Xero appear in PayTrade for reconciliation
  • Map Bank Accounts: Link your Xero bank accounts to PayTrade trust accounts
  • Project Mapping: Associate Xero tracking categories with PayTrade projects

How to Connect

1
Navigate to Integrations

Click "Integrations" in the sidebar menu.

2
Click "Connect Xero"

Click the Xero connection button.

3
Authorise in Xero

You will be redirected to Xero's login page. Sign in and authorise PayTrade to access your Xero organisation.

4
Map Your Accounts

After authorisation, go to the Xero settings page to map your bank accounts and contacts between the two systems.

5
Start Syncing

Once mapped, data will sync automatically. Use the Sync Log to monitor activity and troubleshoot any issues.

Important: Xero integration is only available on Advanced and Pro Audit subscription plans. If you are on Basic or Standard, you will need to upgrade to access this feature.
Tip: Check the Sync Log regularly for any failed sync events. Common issues include contacts without ABNs or invoices with missing fields.

guides.title: Generating and Sending QBCC Notices
guides.content:
Generating and Sending QBCC Notices

QBCC notices are mandatory documents required under the BIF Act. PayTrade generates them as PDFs and sends them to the relevant parties.

Notices list page

Notice Types

What You See on This Page

ComponentWhat It Shows
QBCC TA1 — Account OpeningNotification that a Project Trust Account or Retention Trust Account has been opened. Must be sent when a new trust account is created.
QBCC TA2 — Account ClosingNotification that a trust account has been closed. Sent when a project is completed and the trust account is being wound up.
QBCC TA3 — Related EntitiesDisclosure of related entities for the trust. Required when there are related party transactions.
QBCC TA4 — Part PaymentNotification of a partial payment made from the trust account. Sent when not all beneficiaries receive their full entitlement.
QBCC TA5 — Nil ReturnNotification that no withdrawals were made from the trust account during the reporting period.
S75 Supporting StatementA supporting statement that must accompany payment claims made from a trust account. Generated automatically with each claim.

Generating a Notice

1
Navigate to Notices

Click "Notices" in the sidebar menu.

2
Click "Add Notice"

Click the add button to generate a new notice.

3
Select Notice Type

Choose the type of notice (TA1, TA2, TA3, TA4, or TA5).

4
Select Account and Details

Choose the trust account and fill in any required details.

5
Generate PDF

The system generates the notice as a PDF document. Review it for accuracy.

6
Send Notice

Send the notice to the relevant parties (QBCC, beneficiaries, etc.) via email. The PDF is attached automatically.

Important: Basic plan users must generate notices manually. Standard, Advanced, and Pro Audit users get automated notice generation based on compliance triggers — the system creates notices when events occur that require them.
Tip: All generated notices are stored permanently and can be accessed from the Notices list at any time. This provides a complete audit trail for regulatory purposes.

guides.title: Compliance Monitoring
guides.content:
Compliance Monitoring

PayTrade automatically monitors your compliance with the BIF Act and QBCC requirements. This guide explains how to use the Compliance module.

Compliance Overview page

Compliance Dashboard

What You See on This Page

ComponentWhat It Shows
Project NameThe project being monitored
Account TypePTA or RTA — which trust account is being checked
Status"Ok" (compliant, shown in green) or "Action Required" (issues found, shown in red/orange)
Issues FoundA description of the specific compliance problem detected
Action LinkClick to go directly to the relevant page to resolve the issue

What Compliance Checks Monitor

  • Trust Account Establishment: Is the PTA/RTA opened within the required timeframe?
  • Opening Notices: Has the QBCC TA1 notice been generated and sent?
  • Monthly Reconciliation: Is the trust account reconciled within the required period?
  • Payment Deadlines: Are payments being made within the contractual timeframe?
  • Notice Requirements: Are all required QBCC notices generated and sent?
  • Retention Trust: Is retention money deposited in the correct RTA?
  • Beneficiary Records: Are all trust beneficiaries correctly recorded?

Resolving Compliance Issues

1
Review the Issue

Click on the "Action Required" item to see exactly what needs to be done.

2
Take the Required Action

The system links you directly to the relevant page — for example, if a reconciliation is overdue, it takes you to the Reconciliation Records page.

3
Verify Resolution

After completing the action, return to the Compliance Overview. The status should update to "Ok".

Tip: Check the Compliance dashboard regularly — at least weekly. The dashboard counter on your home screen also shows the total number of items needing attention.

guides.title: Trust Accounting Overview
guides.content:
Trust Accounting Overview

Trust accounting is the backbone of BIF Act compliance. This guide explains every component of the Trust Accounting module.

Trust Accounting dashboard

Trust Accounting Pages

What You See on This Page

ComponentWhat It Shows
Trust Accounting DashboardOverview of all trust accounts, their balances, and compliance status
JournalsEvery financial entry recorded in the trust account — deposits, withdrawals, transfers. Each entry is a double-entry journal (debit and credit).
Account LedgerA detailed view of all transactions for a specific account, showing running balances. Used for auditing and reporting.
Trial BalanceA financial statement listing all account balances for a reporting period. Debits must equal credits — if they don't, there is an error to investigate.
DepositsTrack all deposits into trust accounts, including their source and purpose.
Reconciliation RecordsMonthly reconciliation records comparing the trust account bank balance against the ledger balance.
Audit (Pro Audit Only)External audit tracking as required by QBCC regulations. Record audit dates, findings, and outcomes.

Key Concepts

Journal Entries

Journal entries are created automatically when:

  • A payment claim is processed
  • A bank transaction is matched
  • A deposit is recorded
  • Interest or charges are entered

Monthly Reconciliation

At the end of each month, you must create a reconciliation record that compares:

  • The bank statement closing balance
  • The trust account ledger closing balance
  • Any outstanding (unmatched) items that explain the difference

7-Year Record Retention

Trust account records must be retained for 7 years under the BIF Act. PayTrade stores all records automatically and ensures compliance with this requirement.

Important: Monthly reconciliations are a legal requirement for all trust accounts. The Compliance module monitors whether reconciliations are up to date and alerts you if one is overdue.

guides.title: Uploading and Reconciling Bank Transactions
guides.content:
Uploading and Reconciling Bank Transactions

Reconciliation ensures your trust account records match your actual bank statements. Here's the complete process.

Why Reconciliation Matters

Under the BIF Act, trust account holders must perform monthly reconciliations to ensure the trust account ledger matches the bank statement. PayTrade simplifies this process by allowing you to upload bank transactions and match them against recorded claims and payments.

Step 1: Upload Bank Transactions

1
Open the Account

Navigate to Bank Accounts, then click the account you want to reconcile to open its Overview page.

2
Click "Upload Transactions"

Click the upload button to go to the transaction upload page.

3
Select CSV File

Download your bank statement as a CSV file from your bank, then upload it here. The system parses each transaction row automatically.

4
Review Imported Transactions

Check that all transactions have been imported correctly. The system shows the date, description, amount, and running balance for each.

Step 2: Match Transactions

1
Navigate to Match Transactions

From the account overview, click "Match Transactions".

2
View Unmatched Items

The page shows two columns: unmatched bank transactions (from your CSV) and unmatched claims/payments (from your PayTrade records).

3
Select Matches

Click a bank transaction and the corresponding claim payment to match them together. The amounts should align.

4
Confirm Match

Click "Match" to confirm. The matched pair is removed from the unmatched list, and the trust account ledger is updated.

Step 3: Handle Mismatches

If a match was made incorrectly:

1
Go to Unmatch Transactions

From the account overview, click "Unmatch Transactions".

2
Select the Incorrect Match

Find the incorrectly matched transaction pair.

3
Unmatch

Click "Unmatch" to reverse the match. Both items return to the unmatched list.

Important: All bank transactions should be matched before the monthly reconciliation deadline. Unmatched transactions appear on your dashboard as alerts and may trigger compliance warnings.
Tip: If you have Bank Feeds enabled (Standard plan and above), your transactions can be imported automatically via Open Banking, eliminating the need for manual CSV uploads.

guides.title: Setting Up Bank and Trust Accounts
guides.content:
Setting Up Bank and Trust Accounts

PayTrade manages three types of accounts: Cash Accounts, Project Trust Accounts (PTA), and Retention Trust Accounts (RTA). Here's how to set them up.

Bank Accounts (Current) list page

Account Types

What You See on This Page

ComponentWhat It Shows

Bank Accounts Page

What You See on This Page

ComponentWhat It Shows
Account NameThe name you assigned to the account (e.g., "Brisbane CBD Tower PTA")
Account TypeCash Account, Project Trust Account, or Retention Trust Account
BSB / Account NumberYour bank's BSB and account number for identification
Current BalanceThe balance as per the most recent bank statement or transaction upload
StatusActive, Draft, or Archived
Current / Archived TabsSwitch between active accounts and closed/archived ones
ActionsView overview, edit details, upload transactions, or archive

Creating a New Account

1
Click "Add Account"

Navigate to Bank Accounts and click the add button.

2
Select Account Type

Choose Cash Account, Project Trust Account, or Retention Trust Account.

3
Enter Bank Details

Fill in the account name, BSB number, account number, and the financial institution.

4
Link to Project (Trust Accounts)

For PTA and RTA accounts, select which project this trust account belongs to.

5
Save

Important: After creating a Project Trust Account, you must generate and send a QBCC TA1 (Account Opening) notice. The system will flag this as a compliance requirement.
Tip: Your subscription plan limits the number of trust accounts you can create. Basic and Standard plans allow 2, Advanced allows 10, and Pro Audit allows unlimited. Check your plan if you need more.

guides.title: Understanding and Managing Retention
guides.content:
Understanding and Managing Retention

Retention is a percentage of each payment claim withheld as security. Here's how PayTrade tracks and manages it.

Retention List page

What is Retention?

In construction contracts, a percentage of each progress payment (typically 5-10%) is retained by the payer as security for defects. This retained money is released when contractual milestones are met, such as practical completion or the end of the defects liability period.

Under the BIF Act, retention money for eligible projects must be held in a dedicated Retention Trust Account (RTA).

Retention List Page

What You See on This Page

ComponentWhat It Shows
ContractThe contract the retention relates to
Total RetainedThe cumulative retention amount withheld across all claims
Released AmountHow much retention has been released back to the subcontractor
Balance HeldRemaining retention still being held (Total Retained minus Released)
StatusHeld (still in trust) or Released (returned to the subcontractor)
RTA AccountWhich Retention Trust Account the funds are held in

How Retention is Tracked

1
Automatic Calculation

When a payment claim is created, the system automatically calculates the retention amount based on the contract's retention percentage.

2
Retention Withheld

The retention amount is separated from the claim payment and tracked in the Retention List.

3
Deposited in RTA

If the project requires an RTA, the retained funds must be deposited into the designated Retention Trust Account and reconciled.

Claiming Retention Release

1
Verify Conditions

Confirm that the contractual conditions for retention release have been met (e.g., practical completion, defects liability period expiry).

2
Create a Retention Claim

Navigate to Pay Apps and click "Add Claim". Create a claim specifically for the retention release amount, referencing the original contract.

3
Process the Release

Once approved, the retention payment is recorded, the retained amount is marked as released, and the RTA balance updates accordingly.

4
Reconcile

Match the retention release payment with the bank transaction through the standard reconciliation process.

Important: Failure to deposit retention money into a Retention Trust Account when required is a serious compliance breach under the BIF Act. The Compliance dashboard monitors this automatically.

guides.content:
Payments To Do and Payment History

Stay on top of your payment obligations and track your complete payment history.

The Payments To Do page acts as your financial to-do list. It shows every pending payment across all your projects and contracts, sorted by urgency. Overdue payments are highlighted in red.

guides.title: Submitting and Managing Payment Claims
guides.content:
Submitting and Managing Payment Claims

Payment claims (Pay Apps) are how you request payment for work done or receive claims from your subcontractors. This guide covers both sides of the process.

Payment Claims (Pay Apps) list page

Pay Apps Page

What You See on This Page

ComponentWhat It Shows
Receivable TabClaims you have submitted to receive payment — you are the claimant (subcontractor or head contractor claiming from a principal)
Billable TabClaims submitted to you for payment — you are the payer (head contractor receiving claims from subcontractors)
Claim ReferenceA unique reference number for tracking the claim (e.g., PC-001)
ContractThe contract this claim is made against
Claim AmountThe total amount being claimed for the work period
Retention AmountThe portion of the claim withheld as retention (based on contract retention percentage)
Due DateWhen the payment is due based on the contract payment schedule
StatusDraft, Submitted, Payment Received, Unpaid, or Overdue
ActionsView details, edit (if draft), add payment, or generate S75 statement

Submitting a Payment Claim (As Subcontractor or Head Contractor)

1
Navigate to Pay Apps

Click "Pay Apps" in the sidebar menu.

2
Click "Add Claim"

Click the "Add Claim" button in the top-right corner.

3
Select the Contract

Choose which contract this claim relates to from the dropdown. This automatically links the claim to the correct project, client/supplier, and payment accounts.

4
Enter Claim Details

Fill in the claim amount, description of work completed, and attach any supporting documents (invoices, progress photos, etc.).

5
Submit the Claim

Click "Save" to create the claim. The system generates a unique claim reference number. The claim appears in your Receivable tab and in the other party's Billable tab.

Reviewing a Claim (As Head Contractor or Principal)

1
Go to the Billable Tab

Navigate to Pay Apps and click the "Billable" tab to see claims submitted to you.

2
Open the Claim

Click the claim to view its full details including the amount, supporting documents, and contract terms.

3
Review and Respond

Approve the full amount, partially approve, or dispute the claim with reasons.

Recording a Payment

1
Open the Approved Claim

From the claim view page, click the "Add Payment" button.

2
Enter Payment Details

Record the payment amount, date, and bank reference number.

3
S75 Statement

For trust account claims, an S75 Supporting Statement is automatically generated. This is a legal requirement under the BIF Act.

4
Payment Recorded

The payment appears on the Payments List page and the claim status updates accordingly.

Important: S75 Supporting Statements are mandatory when making payments from a Project Trust Account. The system generates them automatically, but you should review and send them to the relevant parties.
Tip: Use the "Payments To Do" page to see all outstanding payments across all contracts in one place. This helps ensure you never miss a payment deadline.

guides.content:
Setting Up and Managing Contracts

Contracts link your projects to clients, suppliers, and payment accounts. Here's how to set them up correctly.

Contracts list page

Contracts List Page

What You See on This Page

ComponentWhat It Shows

Approved VariationsTotal value of approved variations added to the contract

Creating a New Contract

1
Navigate to Contracts

Click "Contracts" in the sidebar menu.

2
Click "Add Contract"

Click the "Add Contract" button in the top-right corner.

Select the Project

guides.title: Creating and Managing Projects
guides.content:
Creating and Managing Projects

Learn how to create construction projects, check PTA eligibility, and manage project lifecycles.

How to Create a New Project

1
Navigate to Projects

Click "Add Project"

3
Enter Project Details

Fill in the project name, description, your role (Principal, Head Contractor, or Sub Contractor), the site address, and the head contract sum.

Important: Your subscription plan limits the number of projects you can create. Basic and Standard plans allow 1 project, Advanced allows 10, and Pro Audit allows unlimited projects. Attempting to exceed your limit will prompt an upgrade message.

Project Overview

guides.title: How to Sign Up and Create Your Account
guides.content:
How to Sign Up and Create Your Account

Get started with PayTrade in minutes. This guide walks you through every step of the registration process.

PayTrade login and sign-up page

Overview

Creating a PayTrade account is a multi-step process that sets up your personal profile and business entity. Once complete, you'll have full access to all features included in your subscription plan.

What You See on This Page

ComponentWhat It Shows
Sign In Panel (Left)For existing users to log in with their email and password
Join PayTrade Today Panel (Right)For new users — enter your email and choose a password to begin registration
Forgot Password LinkClick to reset your password via email verification
User Agreement & Privacy LinksReview the terms of service and privacy policy before signing up

Step-by-Step Registration

1
Enter Your Email & Password

On the sign-up panel (right side), enter your email address and create a strong password. Your password must include at least 8 characters, one uppercase letter, one lowercase letter, one number, and one special character.

2
Verify Your Email

A 6-digit verification code is sent to your email. Enter it within 20 minutes. If the code expires, click "Resend OTP" to get a new one.

3
Personal Details

Enter your first name, last name, phone number, occupation, and position title. Your address is entered with Google Places autocomplete for accuracy.

4
Profile Photo (Optional)

Upload a profile picture. You can crop and adjust the image. This step can be skipped.

5
Business Profile

Enter your company name, ABN, and entity type. The system checks if your business already exists on PayTrade — if so, you can request to join the existing profile instead of creating a duplicate.

6
Tax Information

Provide your tax-related details including TFN and GST registration status.

7
Company Verification

Upload supporting documents such as your QBCC license and business registration papers.

Important: Your email address becomes your login credential. Make sure you use an email you have access to, as you will need it for password resets and security notifications.

What Happens After Registration

When you complete registration, the system automatically:

  • Creates your user account
  • Sets up your personal company profile
  • Assigns you as the Primary Admin of your company
  • Activates the Free (Basic) subscription plan
  • Redirects you to your dashboard
Tip: If you want to upgrade to a paid plan for more features like unlimited projects or Xero integration, you can do so at any time from your Subscription settings.
